q: What status code does RFC 9110 define for 'Misdirected Request'?
Which RFCs does this document list as obsoleted in section 1.4?
gold: RFC 2818 (HTTP Over TLS); RFC 7230 (HTTP/1.1 Message Syntax and Routing, partially); RFC 7231 (HTTP/1.1 Semantics and Content); RFC 7232 (HTTP/1.1 Conditional Requests); and (per appendix change list / full §1.4 table) related prior specs including RFC 7235, RFC 7538, RFC 7615, and RFC 7694

q: List every HTTP method defined in RFC 9110 with whether it is safe and idempotent.
gold: GET: safe, idempotent; HEAD: safe, idempotent; POST: not safe, not idempotent; PUT: not safe, idempotent; DELETE: not safe, idempotent; CONNECT: not safe, not idempotent; OPTIONS: safe, idempotent; TRACE: safe, idempotent

q: Which Menabrea paper did Lovelace translate, and in what year were her notes published?
gold: She translated Luigi Federico Menabrea's paper on Babbage's Analytical Engine (Sketch of the Analytical Engine); her expanded notes were published in 1843

q: Gather every honor, award, or commemoration named after Ada Lovelace mentioned here.
gold: The Ada programming language; roads, buildings, and institutes named after her; programmes, lectures, and courses; plaques, statues, paintings; literary and non-fiction works about her

q: What mass of plastic is estimated to be in the patch, and by which study?
gold: About 80,000 metric tons (88,000 short tons; also stated as ~79 thousand metric tons) with ~1.8 trillion pieces — Ocean Cleanup estimate (published March 2018)

q: List every cleanup effort or organization mentioned and what it attempted.
gold: Ocean Cleanup: mapped/estimated the patch and pursued cleanup of plastics; Ocean Voyages Institute/Project Kaisei: funded/participated in SEAPLEX research, 2010 expedition testing prototype cleanup devices, 2012 tsunami-debris survey voyages; Coastal Conservancy, Earth Day, Ocean Cleanup, and World Cleanup Day: efforts to slow land-generated debris and marine debris accumulation; Ocean Conservancy: reported major country sources of plastic dumping (advocacy/reporting rather than at-sea cleanup)

q: In which year and journal did Rudolf Kálmán publish the original filter paper?
gold: 1960 (Kalman 1960); the original paper is the classic Journal of Basic Engineering (ASME) publication — year is explicit in the article text as Kalman (1960)

q: List every named variant or extension of the Kalman filter described in the article.
gold: Simple Kalman filter (Kalman's original formulation); Kalman–Bucy filter; extended Kalman filter (Schmidt's extended filter); unscented Kalman filter; information filter; square-root filters (Bierman, Thornton, and others); distributed/consensus Kalman filtering; phase-locked loop (described as a very common simple Kalman-filter type); belief filtering (Bayes/evidential updates)
